NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  February 23, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:03 p.m. on
February 23, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.

ROLL CALL

  Present: 5 Councilmember:  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember:  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor/:  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. She also noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on
all agenda items, which would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to
the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering
to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by
sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  February 23, 2021

  1.  CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Melching announced the following Closed Session item:

  1.1  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES (Gov. Code Section
  54957): Consultation with Chief of Police and City Attorney (COVID-
  19)

  There were no requests to speak.

  RECESS

  Mayor Khan recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 4:08 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Khan reconvened the meeting at 4:36 p.m. City Attorney Melching, on behalf of
  the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo presented a video highlighting the Orange County Firefighter
  Academy 51 Graduates.

  Councilmember Carroll provided a brief summary of the recent Orange County Joint
  Power Authority meeting, noting the upcoming formation of the Community Advisory
  Committee (to be seated by the end of April); and announced an upcoming Community
  Choice Energy (CCE) workshop consisting of experts from around the state, including
  chairmen/chairwomen from other CCE aggregation entities, staff members, chief
  executive officers, and industry leaders.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  On Friday, February 19, thanks to a partnership between the City and
  MemorialCare, as well as the efforts made by the COVID-19 Task Force, 200
  Irvine seniors received the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine at the Lakeview
  Senior Center. The City hopes to open more opportunities for members of the
  community to get vaccinated in the near future

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  February 23, 2021

  •  The City’s COVID-19 Task Force, in partnership with Orange County 3rd District
  Supervisor Donald Wagner, will be hosting a Virtual Town Hall meeting regarding
  COVID-19 vaccines on Friday, February 26 from 3 to 4:30 p.m. Community
  members are invited to join the Mayor and Supervisor Wagner, along with
  members of the COVID-19 Task Force, including Dr. Clayton Chau, the Orange
  County Health Care Agency Director and County Health Officer, and Dr. Marnie
  Baker from MemorialCare. To register for the meeting, visit cityofirvine.org.
  Questions for the COVID-19 Task Force can be submitted when registering for
  the event. A confirmation e-mail with information about how to join the webinar
  will be provided upon successful registration.

  •  The City Council has been working closely with the South Coast Air Quality
  Management District (SCAQMD) to ensure that any potential risk to residents
  from emissions at the All American Asphalt Plant are identified and addressed.
  The City has consistently stressed the need for SCAQMD to maintain open and
  timely communication with residents. As a result of these efforts, SCAQMD has
  announced that it will hold its second town hall meeting on the topic on
  Wednesday, March 3 at 6 p.m. The meeting will provide an open forum to
  discuss the results of recent air testing efforts and address other questions and
  concerns from the community. Details regarding the online meeting are available
  at aqmd.gov.

  •  Applications for the City’s Emergency Rental Assistance Program will be
  available on Monday, March 8 at 8 a.m. The City, with support from Orange
  County United Way, will be allocating $17.7 million in state and federal funding to
  help residential renters who have experienced financial setbacks due to the
  COVID-19 pandemic. Applications will be available on the City’s website and
  must be submitted by 5 p.m. on Friday, March 19. A lottery system will be used
  to select grant recipients in order to provide equitable access for all applicants.
  For information on eligibility and additional program details, visit
  cityofirvine.org/erap.

  •  Local Irvine teen Jordan Szigeti-Larenne discovered a need by those unsheltered
  and founded “Homes2Go”, a mobile cart system with a bed, toilet and storage.
  These carts were built in his garage. A Los Angeles based veterans group has
  expressed interest in ordering 30 carts, and Jordan is in the process of raising
  funds to build these carts.

  •  Nithin Parthasarathy from Northwood High School; Amita Ramanujan from
  Portola High School; and high school students Celeste Webb, Richard Lyu,
  Kathleen Pan, and David Xing, were recognized for their Zero Waste Initiative.
  The group coordinated with local store managers to donate food surplus. In the
  past year, food waste valued at over $95,000 was saved and helped serve
  thousands of people in need during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  February 23, 2021

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Carroll, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Kim, and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1
  through 2.4, and 2.7. Item Nos. 2.5 and 2.6 were removed for separate
  discussion.

  2.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of a special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on January 26, 2021.
  2) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on January 26, 2021.

  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING  CERTAIN  CLAIMS  AND  DEMANDS  AND
  SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO
  BE PAID

  1) Approved the construction plans, specifications and contract
  documents for Bridge Rehabilitation Improvements, Capital

  2) Approved the Engineer’s Estimate, Construction Contingency

  3) Authorized staff to solicit competitive bids and award the

  bidder, in accordance with the City’s purchasing policies and

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that while a list or matrix did not

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the adoption of the

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Councilmember
  Agran, to:

  FOR GROCERY WORKERS

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6

  AYES:  3  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Agran, Kim and Khan

  NOES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll and Kuo

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  2.7  COVID-19  SITUATIONAL UPDATE,  EMERGENCY  RENTAL

  ACTION:
  1) Received updates from staff on COVID-19 related
  developments, including community outreach plan for the

  2) Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-08 - A RESOLUTION OF THE

  Prior to recess, Mayor Khan announced that general public comments on items not

  Mayor Khan recessed the meeting at 5:15 p.m.

  RECONVENE

  Mayor Khan reconvened the meeting at 5:25 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE – IRVINE POLICE COLOR GUARD

  Mayor Khan asked Police Chief Hamel to introduce the Irvine Police Color Guard and

  Mayor Khan invited Pastor Jorge Molina from Mariner’s Church to provide the

  Catherine Song performed the National Anthem, followed by Irvine High School student

  STATE OF THE CITY ADDRESS

  Prior to the State of the City Address, Mayor Khan presented a brief video provided by

  RECONVENE

  Mayor Khan reconvened the meeting at 6:15 p.m.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  •  Kyle Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Alejandro, Orange County resident
  •  Dinorah Hernandez, UCI student
  •  Andrea, Orange County resident

  The following individuals spoke in support of building the Veterans Cemetery at the

  •  Jane Roschmann, Irvine resident
  •  Carol Smith, Irvine resident
  •  Pam Smith
  •  Steve Berger

  Dee Fox, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition to Councilmember Carroll’s use of

  ADJOURNMENT
